ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is a transformer, the primary side is labeled u1, and the secondary side is labeled u2; the two ends of the secondary side are connected to a bridge rectifier circuit on the right composed of four diodes. The output end of the bridge rectifier is connected to a load resistor RL, the output voltage u0 is labeled across the load, and no filter capacitor or inductor is seen in the figure. Reasoning: This circuit can be determined to be an ideal single-phase bridge full-wave rectifier circuit. If the RMS value of the transformer secondary voltage is U2, then the peak value of the secondary sinusoidal voltage is sqrt(2)U2. After bridge rectification, the load voltage is a full-wave rectified sine wave, whose average value is U0 = 2Um/pi = 2sqrt(2)U2/pi ≈ 0.9U2. Therefore the relationship between the average value of the output voltage and the RMS value of the transformer secondary voltage is U0 = 0.9U2.
